constraints: Do not modify inputs/flattened_netlist.v or any other file under inputs/; only submission/recovered_rtl.v is graded.
The submission file must be self-contained (single file, no includes of other project files).
The recovered module name and port list must match the interface exactly, or the harness cannot instantiate it and the submission fails.
Only standard, freely available toolchain components (iverilog, vvp, yosys) may be assumed; no proprietary EDA tools.
expected_outputs: A single Verilog file submission/recovered_rtl.v defining module recovered_design with the pinned port list, implementing word-level RTL that is behaviorally (I/O) equivalent to inputs/flattened_netlist.v for every possible input vector, verified by exhaustive/randomized simulation against a generated testbench.

functional_requirements.requirement: recovered_design must compute sum = a + b + c + d (unsigned 32-bit result of adding all four 16-bit operands) for every combination of inputs, matching inputs/flattened_netlist.v output bit-for-bit.

For the specific known vectors a=16'h0001,b=16'h0002,c=16'h0003,d=16'h0004 the output sum must equal 32'h0000000A; for a=16'hFFFF,b=16'hFFFF,c=16'hFFFF,d=16'hFFFF the output sum must equal 32'h0003FFFC.
The submitted file must compile cleanly with iverilog (no syntax errors) and simulate with vvp without runtime errors, instantiated with the exact port list given in the interface section.

The recovered RTL must be purely combinational (no clock/reset ports, no latches, output must be a function of only a,b,c,d) and must not merely instantiate or wrap the original flattened netlist file.

interface: The recovered design MUST be provided in file submission/recovered_rtl.v and MUST define exactly one top-level module named `recovered_design` with this exact port list: `module recovered_design(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input [15:0] c, input [15:0] d, output [31:0] sum);`. Ports: a, b, c, d are four independent unsigned 16-bit input operands (public, no secrets). sum is the unsigned 32-bit output result. No clock or reset ports are used (the design is purely combinational). The same port list and module name are used by inputs/flattened_netlist.v so the harness can instantiate both modules in one testbench and compare outputs cycle-by-cycle (i.e. per input vector) using $monitor/assert style comparison. The submission file must be synthesizable/simulatable standalone (no external dependencies besides standard Verilog).
objective: You are given a flattened, gate-level Verilog netlist (produced by a synthesis/obfuscation flow) that implements some combinational arithmetic function over four 16-bit input buses and produces a single output bus. The netlist has been flattened into primitive gates (AND/OR/XOR/NOT/full-adder-like structures) and all original signal names have been stripped or renamed to generic net labels (e.g. n123, n124...), destroying the original word-level structure. Your task is to analyze the netlist, recover its word-level arithmetic intent, and produce a clean, synthesizable, word-level Verilog RTL module that is functionally equivalent (bit-exact, for all input combinations) to the original flattened design. Submit your recovered RTL as a single self-contained Verilog file.
response_format: A single file at submission/recovered_rtl.v containing valid Verilog-2001 (or SystemVerilog subset supported by iverilog) source defining module recovered_design(input [15:0] a, input [15:0] b, input [15:0] c, input [15:0] d, output [31:0] sum); No other files are graded.
